# Guru Freelance Jobs Scraper

Scrape live freelance job postings from [Guru.com](https://www.guru.com/d/jobs/). Browse jobs with server-side category, keyword, skill, location, budget and sort filters, paginate through the listing, and optionally open every job-detail page for the full description, employer statistics and payment-verification badge. No login, no API key, no cookies required.

## What this actor does

- **Two modes:** `browse` (filtered listing + pagination) and `byJobId` (full job detail pages from URLs)
- **7 top-level categories** covering the whole marketplace, with optional subcategory drill-down
- **Keyword search** through Guru's own keyword/skill path, with a client-side fallback when Guru has no keyword match
- **Skill filters** — keep jobs tagged with every listed skill, applied server-side
- **Location filters** — country names or Guru location paths, applied server-side
- **Budget-type filter** — Fixed Price and Hourly are applied server-side; the combined "Fixed Price or Hourly" value is verified per record
- **Sort order** — newest, oldest, closing soon, budget high/low, hourly rate high/low (budget sorts and hourly-rate sorts are mapped to the equivalent Guru sort when combined with the other budget type)
- **Pagination** — follows Guru's listing pages until `maxItems`, the source total or `maxPages` is reached, with de-duplication by job ID
- **Optional detail enrichment** — `includeDetails: true` adds the full description and employer stats to each browse record
- **Rich per-job data**: skills, budget range, numeric budget bounds and currency, hours/week, project duration, location preference, employer country, quotes received, application deadline
- Automatically engages the free Apify AUTO datacenter proxy if Guru.com temporarily rate-limits direct requests
- Empty fields are always omitted — every field in the output is backed by real scraped data

## Output per job (browse mode)

- `jobId`, `title`, `jobUrl`
- `category`, `categorySlug`, `subcategory`, `subcategorySlug`, `skills[]`
- `description`
- `budgetType`, `budgetRange`, `budgetMin`, `budgetMax`, `budgetCurrency`, `hoursPerWeek`, `duration`, `locationPreference`
- `postedText`, `deadline`, `quotesReceived`
- `employerName`, `employerCountry`
- `scrapedAt`

With `includeDetails: true`, browse records also gain the detail fields below (full description, `employerPaymentVerified`, and one `employer<Stat>` field per row of the employer stats table).

## Output per job (byJobId mode)

`jobId`, `jobUrl`, `title`, `category`, `categorySlug`, `subcategory`, `skills[]`, `skillSlugs[]`, `description`, `postedText`, `deadline`, `quotesReceived`, `budgetType`, `budgetRange`, `budgetMin`, `budgetMax`, `budgetCurrency`, `hoursPerWeek`, `duration`, `locationPreference`, `budgetText`, `employerName`, `employerCountry` (where available), plus:

- `employerPaymentVerified` — `true` when Guru.com shows the "Payment Method Verified" badge for the employer
- `employer<Stat>` — one field per row of the employer's stats table on the job page (e.g. `employerFeedback`, `employerJobsPosted`, `employerTotalSpent`); the exact set of stats present depends on what Guru.com publishes for that employer

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | select | `browse` | `browse` / `byJobId` |
| `category` | select | – | Top-level category, or `all` |
| `subcategory` | string | – | Optional subcategory title or slug |
| `keyword` | string | – | Guru keyword search (server-side, with client-side fallback) |
| `skills` | array | – | Keep jobs tagged with every listed skill (server-side) |
| `locations` | array | – | Country name or Guru location path (`l/india`, `ls/...`, `lc/...`) |
| `sortOrder` | select | `newest` | Newest / oldest / closing soon / budget / hourly-rate sorts |
| `budgetType` | select | `any` | `any` / `Fixed Price` / `Hourly` / `Fixed Price or Hourly` |
| `includeDetails` | boolean | `false` | Also open each job-detail page in browse mode |
| `jobUrls` | array | – | Full job URLs (mode=byJobId) |
| `maxItems` | int | – | Hard cap on emitted records (1–500); prefill `3` |
| `maxPages` | int | – | Hard cap on listing pages crawled (1–50); prefill `1` |
| `proxyConfiguration` | object | AUTO | Only engaged automatically if Guru.com rate-limits |

### Example: browse Programming & Development jobs

```json
{
  "mode": "browse",
  "category": "programming-development",
  "budgetType": "any",
  "maxItems": 40
}
```

### Example: Python jobs with the highest budget first

```json
{
  "mode": "browse",
  "category": "all",
  "keyword": "python",
  "sortOrder": "budget-high",
  "maxItems": 20
}
```

### Example: skills and locations

```json
{
  "mode": "browse",
  "category": "programming-development",
  "skills": ["python", "automation-testing"],
  "locations": ["united-states"],
  "maxItems": 20
}
```

### Example: fetch full detail for specific jobs

```json
{
  "mode": "byJobId",
  "jobUrls": [
    "https://www.guru.com/jobs/dentist-website-in-wordpress/2119938"
  ]
}
```

## Use cases

- **Freelance market research** — track how many jobs post per category and at what budget type
- **Lead generation for freelancers** — pull fresh postings in a skill category to find new clients
- **Rate benchmarking** — compare `budgetMin`, `budgetMax` and `budgetType` across jobs in the same subcategory
- **Employer due diligence** — enable `includeDetails` to check an employer's payment-verification status and posting history before bidding
- **Category trend tracking** — run `category=all` on a schedule to see which categories are most active over time

## FAQ

**Do I need a Guru.com account?** No. All data comes from public listing and job-detail pages.

**How does keyword search work?** Guru's public keyword box is powered by skill pages, so the actor sends the keyword through Guru's own keyword/skill path. If Guru returns no match for a phrase, the actor retries the listing without the keyword and filters the fetched jobs locally, so broad phrases still work.

**Can I filter by city or state?** Yes, but use the Guru path form for those (`ls/united-states/new-york` for a state, `lc/united-states/new-york/new-york` for a city). A plain value like `India` is treated as a country.

**Why did I get 0 results?** The selected combination may have no active postings, or every fetched record may have been excluded by the budget-type check. Try a broader category, remove the keyword, or widen the location.

**Why do some jobs lack `employerCountry` or `quotesReceived`?** These only appear when Guru.com shows them on the listing or detail page; some employers don't display location, and newly posted jobs may not yet show a quote count.

**Can I fetch a job by bare numeric ID?** No. Guru.com redirects bare IDs to a login page and requires the SEO slug in the URL (`/jobs/<slug>/<jobId>`). Browse mode already returns complete `jobUrl` values you can paste into `jobUrls`.

**Which sort should I use with an hourly search?** Guru only offers budget sorts for Fixed Price jobs and hourly-rate sorts for Hourly jobs. Pick either one — when the choice doesn't match the budget type, the actor automatically uses the equivalent sort Guru honours, so hourly jobs still come back highest/lowest rate first.

**How deep can pagination go?** Guru reports the total for each filter and stops surfacing listings past that point. The actor follows every page until `maxItems`, the reported total or `maxPages` is reached, and says so in the run status when the cap is hit.

**When would I need the proxy configuration?** Only if Guru.com temporarily rate-limits direct requests from Apify's infrastructure — the default free datacenter group is usually enough.

**Is this affiliated with Guru.com?** No, this is an independent third-party actor that reads Guru.com's public job pages. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Guru.com, Inc.
